strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy special-value bug in scipy.optimize.curve_fit: with nan_policy="omit" and sigma provided, NaN-corresponding entries are not omitted from sigma on buggy revision, causing a sigma shape ValueError. Use the project’s own regression test (test_curvefit_omitnan) so it fails on the buggy commit and passes on the fixed one.

pinned_because: Bug is observed for SciPy 1.14.1 (confirmed in issue reproducer context)
Bug is observed with NumPy 2.1.2 (confirmed in issue reproducer context)

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision (commit 9285a8bc63ed), running the test_curvefit_omitnan parametrizations fails because curve_fit(exponential, x, y, p0=p0, sigma=sigma, nan_policy="omit") raises ValueError("`sigma` has incorrect shape.") instead of returning results matching the manually-deleted reference. On the fixed revision, all sigma_dim cases pass because sigma is sliced to omit the same indices corresponding to NaNs before shape checking, so curve_fit succeeds and res_opt/res_cov match ref_opt/ref_cov.
strategy.numerical_probe: Trigger is not a numeric value assertion; the oracle is successful execution and equality to reference outputs after omitting indices. The failing probe is the exception raised by curve_fit when sigma slicing is wrong under nan_policy="omit".

input_output_examples.input: From the repository test snippet: rng = np.random.default_rng(578285731148908); N=100; x=np.linspace(1,10,N); y=exponential(x,0.2,0.5) plus noise; choose i_x=rng.integers(N,size=5), i_y=rng.integers(N,size=5); set x[i_x]=np.nan and y[i_y]=np.nan; call curve_fit(exponential, x, y, p0=[0.1,1.0], sigma=sigma, nan_policy="omit") for sigma_dim in {0,1,2}
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Raises ValueError("`sigma` has incorrect shape.") for at least one sigma_dim (typically when sigma is array-like and shape checking occurs after omission).
input_output_examples.expected_output: No exception; res_opt/res_cov returned by curve_fit match those returned by the reference call curve_fit(exponential, x_deleted, y_deleted, p0=p0, sigma=sigma_deleted) where i_delete=np.unique(concat(i_x,i_y)) and x/y/sigma are deleted accordingly.

risks: To make the test fail/pass transition, you must run against the specific SciPy buggy commit 9285a8bc63ed and the corresponding fixed commit from the PR (not provided in the evidence). Installing from PyPI SciPy 1.14.1 alone may or may not correspond to that exact commit depending on packaging/release state.
The failure mode is exception-based; if your environment/commit version doesn’t include the buggy logic, the test may pass even with identical Python/NumPy versions.

The environment specifies OpenBLAS via scipy-openblas (DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY Zen MAX_THREADS=64). This bug is in Python-level sigma omission logic, so BLAS/LAPACK should not matter, but if you change to a different BLAS backend/compile flags and the code path differs, behavior could vary.

This test is in SciPy’s source tree; ensure you run pytest from a SciPy checkout where you can checkout the buggy and fixed revisions. If instead you run the test against installed SciPy package files that don’t match your checkout commit, results won’t reflect the transition you intend to measure.

oracle.reference_source: The regression test itself: compare res_opt/res_cov to ref_opt/ref_cov computed by manually deleting indices i_delete from x, y, and sigma and calling curve_fit without nan_policy.
oracle.why: The test uses assert_allclose with atol=1e-14 for popt and covariance; the critical transition is whether curve_fit with nan_policy="omit" and sigma provided succeeds and matches the reference. The buggy behavior prevents success by raising ValueError due to sigma shape mismatch.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion sees failure because curve_fit(exponential, x, y, p0=p0, sigma=sigma, nan_policy="omit") raises ValueError("`sigma` has incorrect shape.") rather than returning (res_opt, res_cov) that can be compared to the reference results; hence the test fails during execution for the parametrized case(s).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The test proceeds: curve_fit with nan_policy="omit" returns res_opt/res_cov, and they match ref_opt/ref_cov from the reference curve_fit call after manually deleting NaN-corresponding indices from x/y/sigma; both assert_allclose checks pass for all sigma_dim values.
